title: Principal Investigator, Mean Reversion Lab
verdict_why: Only 3 lab notes on record (need >= 50) — not enough history for any scientific verdict. I keep watching the snap-back.
verdict_plain: Reah's verdict: hold and keep watching. The snap-back evidence so far is neither strong enough to apply nor weak enough to withdraw — the watch stays open.
model_gates: APPLY_CANDIDATE nominates only. Adoption requires the runner's champion/challenger gates: held-out Brier improvement ≥ 2e-4, positive in both halves, family-wise α=0.05 with Bonferroni correction, ≥24h between adoptions. WITHDRAW recommends reversionWeight 0. This file never changes a weight directly.

hypotheses.claim: After an expressive 5-minute XRP move, the next move partially snaps back — fading the last bar aligns with subsequent direction more often than chance.
hypotheses.prediction: decisive fading regimes align with 24h direction more often than chance

hypotheses.claim: The mean-reversion member beats the baseline forecast out-of-sample on Brier score.
hypotheses.prediction: member Brier < baseline Brier over n ≥ 200 scored forecasts

hypotheses.claim: The snap-back is stronger after aggressive, high-volume bars — compensated liquidity provision is the mechanism, not noise.
hypotheses.prediction: decisive fades cluster after above-median-volume bars and score better there
hypotheses.test: aggressive-bar rate and conditional scoring from lab notes

hypotheses.claim: The reversion read expresses itself often enough to matter — not a once-a-quarter curiosity.
hypotheses.prediction: decisive_frac ≥ 0.40 over rolling history once n ≥ 100

disciplines_applied.assessment: the average absolute last-bar move in the record is 7.2 bps; I fade 66.7% of cycles. A snap-back is an estimate with error bars, not a law — most moves are noise, and the record says how often I actually speak.
No edge to explain — and I will not pretend a quiet drift was ever a fadeable move.

The fade is built from log returns of the most recent closed bars — change which bars count as "recent" and the number changes, so the window is part of the result. Error propagates: a bias built from a move and a volume read is not twice as certain as either.
When in doubt I vote HOLD: adopting noise corrupts every forecast it touches, and that is the costliest error I can make.
Instrument flag: bar data blind 33.3% of cycles — a broken candle masquerades as a violent move unless you check liveness, and I check.

Short-horizon reversal is the most competed edge in crypto — everyone sees the same tape. The gross effect is documented near a basis point, under typical costs; the edge, if any, is in fading only the expressive, aggressive moves and abstaining the rest. That is why no APPLY verdict of mine ever skips out-of-sample proof.
Known: fading 66.7% of cycles, decisive 66.7%, aggressive-volume share 66.7%. Unknown: whether the snap-back survives the next volatility regime. Confidence: low — the honest answer.
